newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares buoyed by U.S., set new record close.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares buoyed by U.S., set new record close.

text.p: Norwegian shares climbed higher on Friday to set a new all-time closing high, taking a lead from European and the U.S. markets and also buoyed by an appreciating crown and lower interest rates, dealers said.
The Total share index climbed 0.68 percent, or six points to 885.53 points, the 38th record set this year. Turnover was a hefty 1.01 billion crowns.
Media conglomerate Schibsted attracted an active 108 million crowns of trade after posting healthy nine-month results and announcing a buyout of Denmark's Metronome.
The share climbed five crowns to 103 crowns.
Strength in the Norwegian currency and a firmer debt market fuelled activity in the banking sector.
"Banking shares are just wild. People are buying, buying, buying," said one broker.

Fokus Bank gained 0.20 crowns to 37.90 crowns in 94.3 million crowns of business, while the country's largest bank, Den norske Bank, gained 0.30 crowns to 23 crowns and Christiania Bank put on 0.50 crowns to 18.80 crowns.
"The banks had good results and are benefitting from the money market," said another dealer.
